1: Just as the letter A comes first among all the letters, God comes first in the whole world, as the beginning of everything.
2: What good is all your learning if you do not bow at the feet of God, who knows everything perfectly?
3: People who hold on to the feet of God, who walks upon a flower, will live long and do well on this earth.
4: No trouble will ever come to those who stay close to the feet of God, who wants nothing and dislikes nothing.
5: The two kinds of karma (the good and bad results of our actions) that come from not knowing the truth will not stick to those who gladly praise God’s true greatness.
6: People who stay firmly on the pure and true path of God, who has controlled the desires of the five senses, will live long and well.
7: Unless people hold on to the feet of God, who has no equal, it is very hard for them to get rid of the worries of the mind.
8: Unless people hold on to the feet of God, the kind One who is an ocean of goodness, it is hard for them to swim across the other ocean, the sea of life’s troubles.
9: A head that does not bow at the feet of God, who has eight great qualities, is as useless as an eye that cannot see or an ear that cannot hear.
10: Only those who reach the feet of God can swim across the great ocean of births (being born again and again). No one else can.
11: The world keeps living because rain falls without fail. So rain deserves to be called amrita (the drink that makes the gods live forever).
12: Rain grows the food that people eat. Then rain itself also becomes food for them, as the water they drink.
13: If the sky fails to send rain, hunger will settle inside this wide world circled by the sea and make every living thing suffer.
14: When rain, the world’s great source of riches, does not fall enough, even farmers will stop ploughing their fields.
15: Rain can ruin people, and rain can also lift up again the people it has ruined. Rain does it all.
16: Unless rain falls from the sky, you will hardly see even the tip of a blade of green grass on the earth.
17: Even the huge sea will lose its fullness if the clouds, which draw water up from it, stop giving that water back as rain.
18: If the sky dries up, the festivals and the daily worship offered to the gods here on earth will stop.
19: If the sky stops giving rain, then neither giving to others nor tapas (strict self-discipline) will last anywhere in this wide world.
20: If no one in the world can live without water, then good conduct cannot last without rain either.
21: All the good books agree that the greatness of those who live by strict discipline and have given up their desires should be praised above every other greatness.
22: Trying to measure the greatness of those who have given up worldly life is like trying to count all the people who have ever died on earth.
23: Nothing in this world shines brighter than the greatness of those who have weighed the two kinds of life and chosen to live a life of goodness here.
24: A person who controls the five senses with a strong mind, the way an elephant is guided with a hook, is a seed that will grow into the highest place of all, freedom from rebirth.
25: Indra, the king of the gods in heaven, is proof enough of how powerful a person becomes by controlling the desires of the five senses.
26: Great people do things that are hard to do. Small people cannot do what is hard to do.
27: The whole world is in the hands of the person who fully understands the five senses: taste, sight, touch, hearing and smell.
28: The greatness of wise people whose words always come true is shown on earth by the holy sayings they leave behind.
29: If people who stand on the high hill of good character ever get angry, the person who angered them can hardly be protected, even for a moment.
30: The people called anthanar (holy, wise people) are the truly good ones, because they treat every living thing with a kindness that never stops.
31: Doing what is right brings both respect and riches. So what could be better for any living being than doing right?
32: Nothing helps you more than doing what is right, and nothing hurts you more than forgetting to do it.
33: In every way you can, and without ever stopping, do good wherever good can be done.
34: Keeping your mind free of anything bad is true goodness. Everything else is just noise and show.
35: True goodness is living steadily while staying away from four things: jealousy, greed, anger and harsh words.
36: Do good now, and do not say, ‘I will do it later.’ When you die, the good you did is the friend that does not die with you.
37: No one needs to explain what doing good brings. Just look at the difference between the man carrying a palanquin (a covered chair carried on poles) and the man riding in it.
38: If you do good every day, without letting a single day go by empty, it becomes a stone that blocks the road to being born again.
39: Only happiness that comes from doing right is real happiness. Everything else is not happiness at all, and it brings no respect either.
40: What a person should do is always what is right. What a person should avoid is always what deserves blame.
41: A person who truly lives family life is the steady support, on the right path, of the three other kinds of people who depend on them.
42: A family person supports those who have given up worldly life, those who are poor and hungry, and those who have died.
43: The main duty of a family person is to care properly for five: ancestors who have died, the gods, guests, relatives, and themselves.
44: If a family is careful never to do wrong and shares its food with others, its family line will never die out.
45: If family life has love and goodness, then that is both its true nature and its reward.
46: If a person lives family life in the right way, what more could they gain by leaving it for some other path?
47: A person who lives family life the way it should be lived is the best of all who try to do good.
48: A family life that helps others stay on the right path, and never turns from what is right itself, is stronger than the hard self-discipline of hermits.
49: Family life is what is truly called the good life. The other life, of giving up the world, is also good, as long as no one can find fault with it.
50: A person who lives on this earth the way people should live will be counted among the gods in heaven.
51: A true wife has the good qualities a home needs and runs the home within what her husband earns.
52: If a wife does not have the good qualities a home needs, then however grand a man’s life may be, it is worth nothing.
53: If a man’s wife is truly good, what does he lack? If she is not, what does he really have?
54: What could be greater than a woman who has karpu (a strong and faithful mind)?
55: A wife who worships no god but her husband, and honours him as she rises each day, can say ‘Let it rain,’ and the rain will fall.
56: A true wife takes care of herself, looks after her husband, protects the family’s good name, and never grows tired of doing these things.
57: What good is it to lock women up and watch them? The best guard is the one women keep over themselves with their own strong mind.
58: Wives who faithfully honour their husbands will win great praise in the world of the gods.
59: A man whose wife does not care about the family’s good name cannot walk proudly, like a lion, in front of people who mock him.
60: The wise say a good wife is the blessing of a home, and good children are the fine jewels of that blessing.
61: Of all the good things a person can have, we know nothing greater than children who have learned what is worth knowing.
62: If you have children of good character whom no one can blame, no harm will come near you in all seven births (all your lives to come).
63: The wise say children are their parents’ true treasure, and whatever good they gain comes to them through their own actions.
64: Plain rice that your own children have stirred with their small hands tastes far sweeter than amrita (the drink of the gods).
65: Touching your children is a joy to your body, and hearing them talk is a joy to your ears.
66: ‘The flute is sweet, the harp is sweet,’ say only those who have never heard the baby talk of their own children.
67: The best thing a father can do for his son is to make him good enough to sit in the front row among learned people.
68: When children become wiser than their parents, it brings joy not only to the parents but to everyone on this great earth.
69: A mother who hears people call her son a good and wise man feels more joy than she did on the day he was born.
70: The best thing a son can do for his father is to live so well that people ask, ‘What great good did his father do to have such a son?’
71: Is there any lock that can keep love hidden? The small tears of loving people, when someone dear is suffering, will show it to everyone.
72: People without love keep everything for themselves. People with love feel that even their own bones belong to others.
73: The wise say our precious life is joined to a body of bone and flesh for one reason: so it can live a life of love.
74: Love makes us warmly eager to be close to others. That eagerness then brings friendship, a treasure greater than anything we could go looking for.
75: The wise say that the happiness and success people enjoy in this world come from living a life of love.
76: Only foolish people say that love helps only in doing good. Love also gives strength for brave action against wrong.
77: Just as the hot sun burns a worm, which has no bones, goodness itself burns a life that has no love in it.
78: A life without love in the heart is like a dead, dried-up tree in a desert trying to grow green leaves.
79: What use are all the outer parts of the body to people who lack love, the body’s most important inner part?
80: A body that lives with love is truly alive. For people without love, the body is just bones covered with skin.
81: People build a home, look after it, and keep its things safe for one main reason: to welcome guests and take good care of them.
82: Eating alone while a guest waits outside is not right, even if the food were a medicine that stops death.
83: A family that welcomes guests every single day will never be ruined by doing it.
84: Lakshmi, the goddess of good fortune, gladly makes her home in the house of someone who welcomes good guests with a smiling face.
85: Does a person who feeds guests first and eats only what is left even need to sow seeds in their field?
86: A person who cares for the guest who is leaving and watches the road for the next guest will be a welcome guest of the gods in heaven.
87: The good that comes from the holy offering of caring for guests has no fixed size. It is as great as the worth of the guest you serve.
88: Those who never cared for guests will one day cry, ‘We worked hard and saved, but now we have nothing to hold on to.’
89: Being poor while having plenty is what happens when you refuse to welcome guests. Such foolishness is found only in fools.
90: The anicham flower (a very delicate flower) wilts when you just smell it. A guest wilts just as fast when you look at them with a cold, turned-away face.
91: Truly sweet words come from people who understand what is right. They are full of warm love and have no trickery in them.
92: A smiling face and kind words are even better than giving gifts with a happy heart.
93: A welcoming face, a kind look, and sweet words that come from the heart: that is true goodness.
94: People who speak words that make everyone happy will never suffer the pain of poverty.
95: Being humble and speaking kindly are a person’s true jewels. Nothing else deserves to be called a jewel.
96: If a person thinks about what is truly good and then says it kindly, wrongs will fade away and goodness will grow.
97: Words that truly help the listener and never go against good manners bring the speaker both goodwill and good results.
98: Kind words with no meanness in them bring joy both in this life and in the next.
99: Why would someone who has seen the joy kind words bring use harsh words instead?
100: Speaking hurtful words when kind words are ready to use is like picking unripe fruit when ripe fruit hangs right there.
101: Help given to you when you had done nothing for the helper is so great that even earth and heaven together could not repay it.
102: Help given at the right time, when it is truly needed, may be small, but it is worth more than the whole world.
103: When someone helps you without thinking about what they will get back, the goodness of that help, if you weigh it, is bigger than the sea.
104: People who know the value of help see even a tiny favour, as small as a millet seed, as big as a palm tree.
105: The worth of help is not measured by the help itself. It is measured by the goodness of the person who receives it.
106: Never forget the friendship of good, pure-hearted people. Never leave the friendship of those who stood by you in hard times.
107: Good people remember, through all seven births (all their lives to come), the friendship of those who wiped away their sorrow.
108: It is not good to forget a kindness done to you. But it is good to forget a wrong done to you that very same day.
109: Even if someone who once helped you later hurts you terribly, like a killing blow, the pain goes away when you remember the one good thing they did.
110: People who destroy any other kind of goodness may still be saved. But there is no saving the person who is ungrateful for help they were given.
111: Being fair is truly good when a person treats everyone rightly, whether they are enemies, strangers or friends.
112: The riches of a fair-minded person do not fall apart. They last and support even their children and grandchildren.
113: Even if it seems to bring only good, give up any gain that comes from being unfair, that very same day.
114: Whether a person was fair or unfair will be shown by what they leave behind after they die, such as their good or bad name.
115: Loss and gain come in every life. The jewel of good people is a mind that stays fair in both.
116: If your heart leaves fairness and turns to doing wrong, take it as a sure sign: ‘I am going to be ruined.’
117: When a fair person who does what is right becomes poor, the world does not see it as a fall.
118: Like a weighing scale that first sets itself level and then weighs things exactly, a good person stays steady and does not lean to either side. This is their true jewel.
119: Words without bias count as true fairness only when the heart is also firmly free of bias.
120: For traders, the right way to trade is to protect other people’s goods and interests as carefully as their own.
121: Self-control lifts a person up to live among the gods. A lack of it pushes them into a deep darkness they cannot escape.
122: Guard self-control like a treasure, because no living being has anything that does more good than this.
123: If a person knows that self-control is wise and lives with it in the right way, good people will notice, and it will bring them respect.
124: A person who controls themselves and never leaves their proper path in life stands taller than a mountain.
125: Being humble is good for everyone. But in rich people, humility shines like a second kind of riches.
126: If, in one life, a person can pull in their five senses the way a tortoise pulls in its legs, that power will protect them for seven births (all their lives to come).
127: Whatever else you fail to guard, guard your tongue. If you do not, you will suffer because of the mistakes in your own words.
128: If even one word you speak hurts someone through its meaning, all the good you have done becomes useless.
129: A burn from fire heals inside, but a wound made by the tongue never heals.
130: Goodness itself waits on the path, looking for the right time to meet the person who controls anger, has learned much, and stays self-controlled.
131: Good behaviour is what makes a person truly great. So guard it even more carefully than your own life.
132: Work hard to guard your good behaviour. Think about everything else, and you will find that good behaviour is the only friend that truly stays with you.
133: Having good behaviour is what makes a person’s family noble. Losing it turns their birth into a low one.
134: A Brahmin (a member of the priestly class) who forgets the Vedas (holy texts) can learn them again. But if he loses the good behaviour of his birth, his birth itself is ruined.
135: Just as riches never stay with jealous people, greatness never comes to people without good behaviour.
136: Strong-minded people never slip in their behaviour, because they know the trouble a slip brings.
137: Through good behaviour people become great. Through bad behaviour they earn a shame they never needed to suffer.
138: Good behaviour is the seed of good things. Bad behaviour always brings sorrow.
139: People with good behaviour cannot speak bad words, not even by mistake.
140: People who have not learned to live well with the world are foolish, no matter how many books they have read.
141: People who truly understand right and wrong, and how the world works, are never so foolish as to desire another man’s wife.
142: Of all people who do wrong, no one is a bigger fool than the man who stands at another man’s door, wanting his wife.
143: People who plan evil against the family of someone who trusts them completely are no better than dead.
144: However great a man may be, what is his greatness worth if he goes after another man’s wife without thinking even a little about how wrong it is?
145: A man who goes after another man’s wife, thinking it is easy, earns a shame that never dies and stays with him forever.
146: Hatred, sin, fear and shame: these four never leave a man who wrongs another man’s home.
147: A man who does not desire a woman who belongs to another is the one called a true family man, living the right way.
148: For good people, the great courage of not even looking at another man’s wife with desire is not just goodness. It is the fullness of right living.
149: In this world circled by the fearsome sea, who truly deserves every good thing? Those who do not touch a woman who belongs to another man.
150: Even if a man does not live by what is right and does many wrong things, it is still good if he does not desire another man’s wife.
